name: Meaning, Terms, and Equivalent Ratios
description: Understand a ratio as a comparison of like quantities and simplify or scale it without changing its value.
script_scope: Define a:b as a/b after quantities are expressed in compatible units; identify antecedent and consequent; reduce a ratio by a common non-zero factor or scale both terms by the same factor. Distinguish a ratio from a difference and preserve the order of compared quantities. Include conversion of mixed units (such as rupees/paise or metres/centimetres), equivalent ratios, and checks by simplifying or reconstructing the original quantities. Ground the lesson in the chapter’s opening concepts, solved examples 1–3, and objective patterns on comparing counts, lengths, money, and other quantities.

name: Proportion and Missing Proportionals
description: Use equality of ratios and cross-products to find a missing term or proportional mean.
script_scope: Define a:b::c:d as equality a/b=c/d where denominators are non-zero; name means and extremes and derive the product rule ad=bc. Find fourth proportional d, third proportional c, and positive mean proportional √(ab) where the domain permits; include fractional and decimal terms and distinguish a mean proportional from an arithmetic mean. Check every result in the original proportion and reject invalid zero-denominator cases. Use opening concepts and solved examples 3 and 14–15 plus objective questions asking for missing terms or proportional means.

name: Comparing and Transforming Ratios
description: Compare ratios and use compounded, duplicate, triplicate, and componendo-dividendo relationships accurately.
script_scope: Compare a:b and c:d by cross-products only after aligning units and positive denominators. Form compounded ratios by multiplying corresponding terms; derive duplicate/triplicate and sub-duplicate/sub-triplicate ratios with domain care. Explain componendo and dividendo from a/b=c/d: (a+b)/(a−b)=(c+d)/(c−d), when denominators are non-zero, and show when this transformation is useful. Use exact equivalent forms and verify transformed equalities algebraically. Ground in the chapter’s Important Concepts and solved examples 9, 11, 13, and the relevant objective patterns.

name: Finding Ratios from Equations and Expressions
description: Translate percentage, linear, and factorized relationships into ratios of unknown quantities.
script_scope: Solve for x:y from equations involving percentages or decimals of variables, linear expressions such as (ax+by):(cx+dy), and polynomial equations that factor into alternative cases. Show how a shared scale factor cancels, preserve sign/domain conditions, and state all valid ratio branches where factorization yields multiple possibilities. Check a proposed ratio by substitution into the original equation, including whether a denominator or expression can be zero. Use solved examples 1, 4–6, 9–11 and objective questions that encode ratios algebraically.

name: Linking Two-Term Ratios into a Multi-Term Ratio
description: Combine overlapping pairwise ratios by matching their shared quantity consistently.
script_scope: Given chains such as A:B and B:C, scale the ratios so the shared term agrees, then combine; repeat for longer chains such as A:B, B:C, C:D. For fractional or decimal ratio terms, clear denominators carefully before scaling. Explain why independently chosen scale factors must be reconciled and show a common-unit ledger. Find requested pairwise ratios and a complete multi-term ratio, then verify each adjacent pair against the givens. Use solved examples 7–8, 21, and objective patterns with several linked people, groups, or quantities.

name: Dividing Totals and Allocating Shares in a Ratio
description: Convert a stated ratio into parts of a known total and solve allocation problems with linked share conditions.
script_scope: Represent parts in ratio a:b:c as ax,bx,cx; use the sum of terms to find x when a total is known and a difference of terms when a difference is known. Handle fractional share statements such as one share being a fraction of another person’s share or of their combined shares by first translating them into equations, then normalize to a common ratio. Check allocations sum to the total and respect the stated ordering. Use solved examples 19–25 and objective patterns involving distribution of money, quantities, and straightforward proportional profit shares; exclude partnership time-weighting.

name: Ratios, Fractions, and Percentage Comparisons
description: Move between ratios, fractions of a whole, and percent comparisons without changing the base.
script_scope: For a:b, distinguish the share a/(a+b) from the comparison a/b; convert each requested part to a percentage using its stated whole. Translate “A is p% of B,” “A exceeds B by p%,” and sequential percentage changes into equations before finding a ratio. Emphasize that “p% more than” reverses differently from “p% less than” because the base changes. Check a ratio-to-percent result by summing complementary parts to 100% and confirming direction. Use solved examples 16–18 and matching objective problems.

name: Unknown Numbers from Ratio, Sum, Difference, or Powers
description: Use a common multiplier to determine quantities when ratios are paired with totals, gaps, or algebraic constraints.
script_scope: Set quantities in a ratio as ax,bx,cx, then use a stated sum, difference, product, or sum of squares to solve for the scale factor. Keep positive and negative roots consistent with the word problem and check integer/count constraints. Include selecting largest/smallest values from an ordered ratio and translating a squared-sum condition without confusing ratio terms with actual values. Verify all original conditions after substitution. Use solved examples 25–26, 33 and objective patterns about numbers, dimensions, and related quantities.

name: Income, Expenditure, Savings, and Related Ratios
description: Build equations for income and expenditure ratios to recover savings or individual amounts.
script_scope: Represent incomes and expenditures with separate scale variables when their ratios differ; savings equal income minus expenditure, not a ratio term itself. Use a stated savings fraction, equal savings, or savings ratio to link the variables and solve the system. For three people, preserve each person’s own percentage spent or saved before combining ratios. Check each computed saving is non-negative when required and that totals reconcile. Use solved examples 27–29 and objective patterns on salaries, expenditures, savings, and group totals; do not expand into unrelated budgeting or partnership time-share methods.

name: Changing Ratios: Additions, Removals, Ages, and Dimensions
description: Solve for an initial quantity when adding, subtracting, or advancing time changes a ratio.
script_scope: Translate each before/after condition using the same underlying quantities and an explicit change amount. For ages, add the same number of years to each person; for dimensions, apply the stated increase/decrease to the correct dimension; for mixtures or counts, adjust only the named component. Equate the new ratio by cross-multiplication, solve the resulting linear system, and check the original and changed ratios. Handle “what must be added to/subtracted from each term” as a common unknown, not as ratio scaling. Use solved examples 30–34 and objective age/count/dimension patterns.

name: Ratios of Coin Values, Costs, and Weighted Quantities
description: Distinguish a ratio of item counts from a ratio of their total values or weighted contributions.
script_scope: When item counts are in a ratio but denominations or unit rates differ, calculate each group’s total value as count×unit value before comparing totals. Likewise, for cost components or attendance-weighted charges, multiply the amount in each category by its stated per-unit quantity and combine only after unit alignment. Explain why count-ratio terms cannot directly stand for money when denominations differ. Check by reconstructing both totals from the common scale factor. Use solved examples 2, 24, 35, 47–48 and related objective patterns.

name: Mixture Composition, Blending, and Replacement
description: Track component amounts separately when mixtures are combined, diluted, or repeatedly replaced.
script_scope: Represent each mixture by component and total quantities; combine milk/water or priced varieties by adding component amounts rather than averaging ratios directly. Solve a target mixture ratio after adding a component, and derive replacement repeatedly: after each withdrawal-and-replacement, the retained original component is multiplied by (1−removed/total). Distinguish equal volumes from equal concentrations and use common units. Verify component totals and ensure each concentration lies within possible bounds. Use solved examples 42–45, 50–51 and objective mixture questions; do not add unrelated profit-and-loss instruction.

name: Direct, Inverse, and Joint Variation
description: Model proportional relationships with constants and use given values to predict unknowns.
script_scope: Define direct variation x∝y as x=ky and inverse variation x∝1/y as xy=k; determine k from a known pair and apply it to a new condition. Extend to powers and combined dependencies, such as x²∝y³ or resistance proportional to length and inversely proportional to radius squared. Explain which quantities are held constant and check the equation using units and a second substitution. Include square-root dependence and proportional cost to square of weight. Use solved examples 36–38 and 41, 46 and matching objective patterns.

name: Weighted Ratios and Multi-Stage Proportional Changes
description: Combine several ratios or percentage changes while preserving each category’s weight.
script_scope: Use the original ratio as common scale terms, then apply category-specific multipliers and simplify the resulting ratio. For weighted averages, total the weighted contributions and divide by the total weight; do not take an unweighted mean of percentages when group sizes differ. Handle changes to multiple cost components, group populations, incomes across years, and per-day output from different worker categories. Show a table with original amount, multiplier, new amount, and units, then verify the final aggregate. Use solved examples 39–40, 47–49 and objective patterns with changing group rates or totals.

name: Integrated Ratio Reasoning and Data Sufficiency
description: Choose the relevant ratio model, combine conditions efficiently, and decide whether given statements determine a unique answer.
script_scope: Integrate two or more chapter skills in fresh problems: chained ratios plus a total, changed ratios plus ages or dimensions, mixture component tracking, variation, or weighted totals. In data-sufficiency reasoning, test each statement alone and then together; demonstrate sufficiency by showing a unique requested value and insufficiency by constructing two valid outcomes. Keep “enough information” distinct from actually calculating the value, and do not infer unstated relationships. Check uniqueness, units, and all original conditions. Use the chapter’s objective exercises and printed pages 472–474 data-sufficiency section as source patterns; do not extract question banks.
